subproblem.title: Dilation invariance of an integer multiplicity cone: mass scaling, support and density
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) be integer multiplicity (IsIntegerMultiplicity C) and a cone (IsConeCurrent C: currentEval(η_{0,λ#}C, ω) = C(ω) for every λ > 0 and every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P), where η_{0,λ#}C = blowUp C 0 λ). Then for every real s > 0: (1) M_{sW}(C) = ofReal(s^n)·M_W(C) for every set W ⊆ ℝ^P, where sW = {s·x : x ∈ W} and M_W = massOn (values in [0, ∞]); (2) s·x ∈ spt C if and only if x ∈ spt C, for every x ∈ ℝ^P; (3) HasMassDensity C (s·x) θ if and only if HasMassDensity C x θ, for every x ∈ ℝ^P and θ ∈ ℝ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), IsIntegerMultiplicity C → IsConeCurrent C → ∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), C.massOn ((fun x => s • x) '' W) = ENNReal.ofReal (s ^ n) * C.massOn W) ∧ (∀ x : Euclid P, s • x ∈ C.support ↔ x ∈ C.support) ∧ ∀ (x : Euclid P) (θ : ℝ), HasMassDensity C (s • x) θ ↔ HasMassDensity C x θ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: paragraph (K) "Cone facts" of the parent proof of idtp_two_dim_cone_integer_density (Departure [D3] of that proof: the book, chapter-07.txt lines 497–510, gives no proof). Conventions: ℝ^P = Euclid P; B_r(x) = ball x r; for a current T on a domain D and W ⊆ ℝ^P, M_W(T) = T.massOn W is the supremum in [0, ∞] of ofReal(T(ω)) over ω ∈ 𝒟^n(D) (test forms with tsupport ω ⊆ D) such that tsupport ω ⊆ W and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(y)) ≤ 1 for all y; ω_n = unitBallVolume n; η_{x,λ} = dilation x λ, η_{x,λ}(y) = −(λ⁻¹x) + λ⁻¹y.
1. Fix s > 0 and let λ := s⁻¹ > 0. Then η_{0,λ}(y) = −(λ⁻¹·0) + λ⁻¹y = s·y for every y. Hence η_{0,λ}(W) = sW for every W ⊆ ℝ^P, and D := η_{0,λ}(ℝ^P) = ℝ^P, because every y equals η_{0,λ}(s⁻¹y). Let B := blowUp C 0 λ ∈ 𝒟_n(D).
2. (B and C have the same local masses.) Let V ⊆ ℝ^P. The elements of 𝒟^n(D) are the forms ω with IsTestForm ω and tsupport ω ⊆ D = ℝ^P; these are exactly the underlying forms of the elements of 𝒟^n(ℝ^P), and the admissibility conditions defining M_V (tsupport ω ⊆ V and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(y)) ≤ 1 for all y) depend only on the underlying form. For such an ω the condition IsTestForm ω ∧ tsupport ω ⊆ D holds, so currentEval(B, ω) = B(ω) by the definition of currentEval, and IsConeCurrent C (for this λ > 0) gives currentEval(B, ω) = C(ω). Hence the sets {ofReal(B(ω))} and {ofReal(C(ω))}, ω ranging over the M_V-admissible forms, are equal, and M_V(B) = M_V(C) for every V ⊆ ℝ^P.
3. (Conclusion (1).) The accepted theorem Submission.dtc_blowUp_massOn_image (U := ℝ^P, T := C, x := 0, lam := λ, and the given W) gives M_{η_{0,λ}(W)}(B) = ofReal((λ⁻¹)^n)·M_W(C). By step 1, η_{0,λ}(W) = sW and λ⁻¹ = s; by step 2, M_{sW}(B) = M_{sW}(C). Therefore M_{sW}(C) = ofReal(s^n)·M_W(C).
4. (Balls.) For x ∈ ℝ^P and r > 0, s·B_{r/s}(x) = B_r(s·x): |s·y − s·x| = s|y − x| < r if and only if |y − x| < r/s, and every z ∈ B_r(s·x) equals s·(s⁻¹z) with s⁻¹z ∈ B_{r/s}(x). By (1), M_{B_r(s·x)}(C) = ofReal(s^n)·M_{B_{r/s}(x)}(C), and ofReal(s^n) ∈ (0, ∞).
5. (Conclusion (2).) Choose an IMRep R of ℝ^P with R.Represents C (IsIntegerMultiplicity C) and let μ := R.measure. The accepted theorem Submission.dimred_im_mass_measure (U := ℝ^P, which is open, T := C) gives (a) M_W(C) = μ(W) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P, and (b) y ∈ spt C if and only if μ(B_ε(y)) ≠ 0 for every ε > 0. By step 4 and (a), μ(B_r(s·x)) = ofReal(s^n)·μ(B_{r/s}(x)) for every r > 0; since ofReal(s^n) ∈ (0, ∞), μ(B_r(s·x)) ≠ 0 if and only if μ(B_{r/s}(x)) ≠ 0. As r runs through (0, ∞), so does r/s. By (b), s·x ∈ spt C if and only if x ∈ spt C.
6. (Conclusion (3).) For ρ > 0 let f(ρ) := M_{B_ρ(s·x)}(C)/(ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n)) and g(ρ) := M_{B_ρ(x)}(C)/(ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n)). Since ρ^n = s^n·(ρ/s)^n with both factors ≥ 0, ofReal(ρ^n) = ofReal(s^n)·ofReal((ρ/s)^n). By step 4 and cancellation of the common factor ofReal(s^n) ∈ (0, ∞) in numerator and denominator (ENNReal.mul_div_mul_left), f(ρ) = g(ρ/s) for every ρ > 0, and likewise g(t) = f(s·t) for every t > 0. The maps ρ ↦ ρ/s and t ↦ s·t send the filter 𝓝[>]0 into 𝓝[>]0. Hence, for every θ, f tends to ofReal θ along 𝓝[>]0 if and only if g does. Since HasMassDensity C y θ means 0 ≤ θ together with the convergence of the corresponding ratio at y to ofReal θ, HasMassDensity C (s·x) θ holds if and only if HasMassDensity C x θ holds. ∎
proof_key_steps: With λ = 1/s, dilation 0 λ is y ↦ s·y and maps ℝ^P onto ℝ^P.
The cone identity makes blowUp C 0 λ and C agree on every admissible test form, so M_V(blowUp C 0 λ) = M_V(C) for all V.
Submission.dtc_blowUp_massOn_image then gives M_{sW}(C) = s^n·M_W(C), in particular M_{B_r(sx)}(C) = s^n·M_{B_{r/s}(x)}(C).
Mass equals the representation measure μ on open sets and spt C = {y : μ(B_ε(y)) ≠ 0 for all ε > 0} (dimred_im_mass_measure), giving sx ∈ spt C ⟺ x ∈ spt C.
The density ratio at sx and radius ρ equals the ratio at x and radius ρ/s, so the densities coincide.

subproblem.title: A closed dilation-invariant set that is locally a 2-plane away from 0 lies in finitely many 2-planes meeting only at 0
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let S ⊆ ℝ^P be a closed set such that s·x ∈ S for every x ∈ S and every real s > 0. Suppose every p ∈ S with p ≠ 0 has δ > 0 and a 2-dimensional linear subspace Q of ℝ^P with S ∩ B_δ(p) = Q ∩ B_δ(p). Then there are q ∈ ℕ and 2-dimensional linear subspaces P_1, …, P_q (a family indexed by Fin q) with P_i ∩ P_j = {0} (P_i ⊓ P_j = ⊥) for all i ≠ j, such that every x ∈ S with x ≠ 0 lies in some P_i.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (S : Set (Euclid P)), IsClosed S → (∀ x ∈ S, ∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → s • x ∈ S) → (∀ p ∈ S, p ≠ 0 → ∃ (δ : ℝ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), 0 < δ ∧ Module.finrank ℝ Q = 2 ∧ S ∩ ball p δ = (Q : Set (Euclid P)) ∩ ball p δ) → ∃ (q : ℕ) (Ps : Fin q → Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), (∀ i, Module.finrank ℝ (Ps i) = 2) ∧ (∀ i j, i ≠ j → Ps i ⊓ Ps j = ⊥) ∧ ∀ x ∈ S, x ≠ 0 → ∃ i, x ∈ Ps i
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 7 of the parent proof (the link Σ = spt C ∩ 𝕊 is a finite disjoint union of great circles; by dilation invariance spt C ∖ {0} lies in the corresponding planes, which pairwise meet only at 0), stated for an arbitrary closed dilation-invariant set that is locally a 2-plane away from 0. Notation: 𝕊 := {x ∈ ℝ^P : |x| = 1}; B_r(x) = ball x r.
0. Σ := S ∩ 𝕊 is compact (a closed subset of the compact sphere, Mathlib isCompact_sphere). For every p ∈ S ∖ {0} fix, by hypothesis, δ_p > 0 and a 2-dimensional subspace Q_p with S ∩ B_{δ_p}(p) = Q_p ∩ B_{δ_p}(p); since p ∈ S ∩ B_{δ_p}(p), p ∈ Q_p.
1. (Uniqueness of planes.) If Q₁, Q₂ are linear subspaces, x ∈ Q₁, t > 0 and Q₁ ∩ B_t(x) = Q₂ ∩ B_t(x), then Q₁ = Q₂. Indeed x ∈ Q₁ ∩ B_t(x) ⊆ Q₂. For v ∈ Q₁ choose 0 < s < t/(|v| + 1); then x + s·v ∈ Q₁ ∩ B_t(x) ⊆ Q₂, so s·v = (x + s·v) − x ∈ Q₂ and v ∈ Q₂. Thus Q₁ ⊆ Q₂, and symmetrically (now x ∈ Q₂) Q₂ ⊆ Q₁.
2. (Points where S is locally a given plane.) For a 2-dimensional subspace Q let Loc(Q) := {x ∈ Q : there is ε > 0 with S ∩ B_ε(x) = Q ∩ B_ε(x)}. Then Loc(Q) ⊆ S (x ∈ Q ∩ B_ε(x) = S ∩ B_ε(x)), and Loc(Q) is open relative to Q: if x ∈ Loc(Q) with ε and x' ∈ Q with |x' − x| < ε, then with ε' := ε − |x' − x| > 0, B_{ε'}(x') ⊆ B_ε(x) and S ∩ B_{ε'}(x') = Q ∩ B_ε(x) ∩ B_{ε'}(x') = Q ∩ B_{ε'}(x'), so x' ∈ Loc(Q).
3. (Whole great circles.) Let Q be a 2-dimensional subspace and K := Q ∩ 𝕊. If Loc(Q) ∩ K ≠ ∅, then K ⊆ Loc(Q). Proof: K is connected, being the image under the continuous inclusion Q → ℝ^P of the unit sphere of the 2-dimensional normed space Q, which is connected by Mathlib isConnected_sphere (rank Q = 2 > 1). Let A₁ := K ∩ Loc(Q) and A₂ := K ∖ Loc(Q). A₁ is relatively open in K by step 2. A₂ is relatively open in K: let x ∈ A₂. If x ∉ S, then, S being closed, some t > 0 has B_t(x) ∩ S = ∅, and K ∩ B_t(x) ⊆ A₂ because Loc(Q) ⊆ S. If x ∈ S, then x ≠ 0 (|x| = 1) and Q_x ≠ Q (otherwise x ∈ Loc(Q) with ε := δ_x). Let x' ∈ K ∩ B_{δ_x/2}(x) and suppose x' ∈ Loc(Q) with some ε'; with t := min(ε', δ_x/2) we have B_t(x') ⊆ B_{δ_x}(x), so Q ∩ B_t(x') = S ∩ B_t(x') = Q_x ∩ B_t(x') and x' ∈ Q, whence Q = Q_x by step 1, a contradiction; so K ∩ B_{δ_x/2}(x) ⊆ A₂. Thus K is the disjoint union of the relatively open sets A₁ ≠ ∅ and A₂, and connectedness gives A₂ = ∅, i.e. K ⊆ Loc(Q).
4. (Great circles through points of Σ.) For p ∈ Σ put K_p := Q_p ∩ 𝕊. Then p ∈ K_p and p ∈ Loc(Q_p) (with ε := δ_p), so K_p ⊆ Loc(Q_p) by step 3.
5. (Two such circles are equal or disjoint.) If p, p' ∈ Σ and K_p ∩ K_{p'} ≠ ∅, then Q_p = Q_{p'}: for x ∈ K_p ∩ K_{p'}, step 4 gives ε, ε' > 0 with S ∩ B_ε(x) = Q_p ∩ B_ε(x) and S ∩ B_{ε'}(x) = Q_{p'} ∩ B_{ε'}(x); with t := min(ε, ε'), Q_p ∩ B_t(x) = Q_{p'} ∩ B_t(x) and x ∈ Q_p, so Q_p = Q_{p'} by step 1.
6. (Finite cover.) The open balls B_{δ_p}(p), p ∈ Σ, cover the compact set Σ, so there is a finite set F ⊆ Σ with Σ ⊆ ⋃_{p∈F} B_{δ_p}(p) (IsCompact.elim_finite_subcover).
7. (The planes.) The set 𝒫 := {Q_p : p ∈ F} of subspaces is finite; let q be its cardinality and P_1, …, P_q an injective enumeration of 𝒫 indexed by Fin q (e.g. via Finset.equivFin). Each P_i equals Q_p for some p ∈ F ⊆ Σ, so finrank P_i = 2.
8. (Pairwise intersections.) Let i ≠ j, so P_i ≠ P_j by injectivity; write P_i = Q_p and P_j = Q_{p'} with p, p' ∈ Σ. If v ∈ P_i ∩ P_j and v ≠ 0, then v/|v| ∈ K_p ∩ K_{p'}, so Q_p = Q_{p'} by step 5, i.e. P_i = P_j, a contradiction. Hence P_i ∩ P_j = {0}, i.e. P_i ⊓ P_j = ⊥.
9. (Covering.) Let x ∈ S with x ≠ 0 and x̂ := |x|⁻¹·x. By the dilation hypothesis (s := |x|⁻¹ > 0), x̂ ∈ S, and |x̂| = 1, so x̂ ∈ Σ. By step 6 there is p ∈ F with x̂ ∈ B_{δ_p}(p), so x̂ ∈ S ∩ B_{δ_p}(p) = Q_p ∩ B_{δ_p}(p), and x = |x|·x̂ ∈ Q_p = P_i for the index i of Q_p in the enumeration. (If Σ = ∅, then F = ∅, q = 0, and there is no such x, because x̂ would lie in Σ.) ∎
proof_key_steps: Two linear subspaces that agree near a common point coincide.
For a plane Q, the set of points of the great circle Q ∩ 𝕊 near which S equals Q is relatively open, and so is its complement (closedness of S, local planarity and uniqueness of planes).
By connectedness of great circles, the circle K_p through each p ∈ Σ = S ∩ 𝕊 lies in S with S locally equal to Q_p along it; hence two such circles are equal or disjoint.
Compactness of Σ gives finitely many planes Q_p whose balls cover Σ; distinct ones meet only in 0 because their circles are disjoint.
Dilation invariance carries the covering of Σ over to S ∖ {0}.

audit.reason: The local-plane uniqueness and clopen great-circle argument are valid. Compactness gives finitely many distinct planes, intersections are reduced to the origin, and positive dilation covers every nonzero point of S. The empty-link case correctly permits q = 0.

subproblem.title: Euclidean Hausdorff measure of a disc in a linear subspace
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let Q ⊆ ℝ^P be a linear subspace with dim Q = n (Module.finrank ℝ Q = n), let y ∈ Q and ρ > 0. Then H^n(Q ∩ B_ρ(y)) = ω_n·ofReal(ρ^n), where H^n = μHE[n] is Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure on ℝ^P and ω_n = unitBallVolume n is the Lebesgue measure of the open unit ball of ℝ^n.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (y : Euclid P) (ρ : ℝ), Module.finrank ℝ Q = n → y ∈ Q → 0 < ρ → μHE[n] ((Q : Set (Euclid P)) ∩ ball y ρ) = unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the conventions of the parent proof ("For a 2-dimensional subspace Q, H²⌞Q is the image of Lebesgue measure of ℝ² under a linear isometry (Mathlib Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume), so H²(Q ∩ B_ρ(y)) = ω_2ρ² for y ∈ Q"), proved here in every dimension n.
1. Let ι : Q → ℝ^P be the inclusion x ↦ (x : ℝ^P). It is an isometry, because the norm of Q is the restriction of the norm of ℝ^P, and its range is Q. By Mathlib Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_preimage, μHE[n](ι⁻¹(B_ρ(y))) = μHE[n](B_ρ(y) ∩ Q), where the left side is the measure μHE[n] of the metric space Q. Also B_ρ(y) ∩ Q = Q ∩ B_ρ(y).
2. Let y₀ := ⟨y, hy⟩ ∈ Q. Since the distance of Q is the restriction of the distance of ℝ^P, ι⁻¹(B_ρ(y)) = B_ρ(y₀), the open ball of Q.
3. Q is a finite-dimensional real inner product space with finrank ℝ Q = n. By Mathlib InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume (μHE[finrank ℝ Q] = volume on Q, the volume of measureSpaceOfInnerProductSpace), rewritten with finrank ℝ Q = n, the measure μHE[n] of Q equals volume.
4. volume on Q is an additive Haar measure, so Mathlib Measure.addHaar_ball_of_pos (ρ > 0) gives volume(B_ρ(y₀)) = ofReal(ρ^{finrank ℝ Q})·volume(B_1(0_Q)) = ofReal(ρ^n)·volume(B_1(0_Q)).
5. Let b be stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ Q reindexed by Fin n (possible since finrank ℝ Q = n) and e := b.repr : Q ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) = Euclid n. By Mathlib LinearIsometryEquiv.measurePreserving, e is measure preserving for the volumes; as e is a linear isometry equivalence, B_1(0_Q) = e⁻¹(B_1(0)) with B_1(0) ⊆ Euclid n. Hence volume(B_1(0_Q)) = volume(ball (0 : Euclid n) 1) = unitBallVolume n.
6. Combining steps 1–5: μHE[n](Q ∩ B_ρ(y)) = μHE[n](B_ρ(y₀)) = volume(B_ρ(y₀)) = ofReal(ρ^n)·unitBallVolume n = unitBallVolume n·ofReal(ρ^n). The argument is uniform in n, including n = 0, where Q = {0}. ∎
proof_key_steps: The inclusion of Q is an isometry, so μHE[n](Q ∩ B_ρ(y)) is μHE[n] of the ball B_ρ(y) of Q.
On the n-dimensional inner product space Q, μHE[n] = volume.
Haar scaling gives volume(B_ρ(y)) = ρ^n·volume(B_1(0_Q)).
A linear isometry Q ≃ Euclid n preserves volume, so volume(B_1(0_Q)) = ω_n.

subproblem.title: Arcs of constant density and plane on a minimizing 2-cone continue until a density jump (sector lemma)
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let C ∈ 𝒟_2(ℝ^P) be minimizing in ℝ^P (IsMinimizingIn C univ), with ∂C = 0 (BoundaryVanishes C) and a cone (IsConeCurrent C). Let Q ⊆ ℝ^P be a 2-dimensional linear subspace, z, e ∈ Q with |z| = |e| = 1 and ⟨z, e⟩ = 0, k ∈ ℕ with k ≥ 1, and L ∈ ℝ; write γ(φ) := cos φ·z + sin φ·e. Assume (i) there is ε > 0 with spt C ∩ B_ε(z) = Q ∩ B_ε(z) and HasMassDensity C y k for every y ∈ spt C ∩ B_ε(z); and (ii) for every φ with 0 < φ < L such that γ(φ) ∈ spt C and HasMassDensity C γ(φ) k, there are δ > 0 and k' ∈ ℕ with HasMassDensity C y k' for every y ∈ spt C ∩ B_δ(γ(φ)). Then for every φ with 0 ≤ φ < L there is ε > 0 with spt C ∩ B_ε(γ(φ)) = Q ∩ B_ε(γ(φ)) and HasMassDensity C y k for every y ∈ spt C ∩ B_ε(γ(φ)).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 2) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (z e : Euclid P) (k : ℕ) (L : ℝ), IsMinimizingIn C univ → BoundaryVanishes C → IsConeCurrent C → Module.finrank ℝ Q = 2 → z ∈ Q → e ∈ Q → ‖z‖ = 1 → ‖e‖ = 1 → inner ℝ z e = 0 → 1 ≤ k → (∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧ C.support ∩ ball z ε = (Q : Set (Euclid P)) ∩ ball z ε ∧ ∀ y ∈ C.support, y ∈ ball z ε → HasMassDensity C y k) → (∀ φ : ℝ, 0 < φ → φ < L → Real.cos φ • z + Real.sin φ • e ∈ C.support → HasMassDensity C (Real.cos φ • z + Real.sin φ • e) k → ∃ (δ : ℝ) (k' : ℕ), 0 < δ ∧ ∀ y ∈ C.support, y ∈ ball (Real.cos φ • z + Real.sin φ • e) δ → HasMassDensity C y k') → ∀ φ : ℝ, 0 ≤ φ → φ < L → ∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧ C.support ∩ ball (Real.cos φ • z + Real.sin φ • e) ε = (Q : Set (Euclid P)) ∩ ball (Real.cos φ • z + Real.sin φ • e) ε ∧ ∀ y ∈ C.support, y ∈ ball (Real.cos φ • z + Real.sin φ • e) ε → HasMassDensity C y k
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 4 and 6 of the parent proof (arcs of Σ_G on which the plane and the density are constant; an endpoint of such an arc lying in Σ_G would extend the arc; the sibling prerequisite cone_sector_endpoint_density forces the arc's density at an endpoint), organised here as a continuity argument along the parametrised great circle γ.
0. Notation and facts. For w ∈ ℝ^P let Good(w) mean: there is ε > 0 with spt C ∩ B_ε(w) = Q ∩ B_ε(w) and HasMassDensity C y k for every y ∈ spt C ∩ B_ε(w). (a) Densities are unique: if HasMassDensity C y θ and HasMassDensity C y θ', then θ = θ' (both are ≥ 0, the limits ofReal θ and ofReal θ' of the same function along 𝓝[>]0 in the Hausdorff space [0, ∞] coincide, and ofReal is injective on [0, ∞)). (b) γ(φ) ∈ Q and |γ(φ)| = 1 (|γ(φ)|² = cos²φ + sin²φ, as |z| = |e| = 1 and ⟨z, e⟩ = 0); γ is continuous and |γ(φ) − γ(ψ)| ≤ |φ − ψ| (|γ(φ) − γ(ψ)|² = 2 − 2cos(φ − ψ) = 4sin²((φ − ψ)/2) ≤ (φ − ψ)²). (c) C is integer multiplicity (first component of IsMinimizingIn C univ), so the sibling idtp_tdc_cone_dilation gives, for every t > 0 and all x, θ: t·x ∈ spt C ⟺ x ∈ spt C, and HasMassDensity C (t·x) θ ⟺ HasMassDensity C x θ. (d) spt C is closed: spt C = ℝ^P ∖ zeroRegion(C), and the zero region is open (GeometricCurrentOn.isOpen_zeroRegion).
1. (Good is an open condition.) If Good(w) holds with ε and |w' − w| < ε/2, then Good(w') holds with ε/2: B_{ε/2}(w') ⊆ B_ε(w), so spt C ∩ B_{ε/2}(w') = (Q ∩ B_ε(w)) ∩ B_{ε/2}(w') = Q ∩ B_{ε/2}(w'), and the density condition on spt C ∩ B_{ε/2}(w') ⊆ spt C ∩ B_ε(w) is inherited.
2. (First failure.) Suppose the conclusion fails, so that A := {φ ∈ [0, L) : Good(γ(φ)) fails} is nonempty, and let φ* := inf A. Then 0 ≤ φ* < L (φ* is at most every element of A, and these are < L), and Good(γ(φ)) holds for every φ ∈ [0, φ*). If Good(γ(φ*)) held with some ε, then by step 1 and (b), Good(γ(φ)) would hold for every φ ∈ [φ*, φ* + ε/2); then A ⊆ [φ* + ε/2, L), so inf A ≥ φ* + ε/2 > φ*, which is absurd. Hence Good(a) fails, where a := γ(φ*). By hypothesis (i), Good(γ(0)) = Good(z) holds, so φ* ≠ 0. Thus 0 < φ* < L, Good(γ(φ)) holds for all φ ∈ [0, φ*), and Good(a) fails.
3. (a ∈ spt C.) For φ ∈ [0, φ*), Good(γ(φ)) with some ε gives γ(φ) ∈ Q ∩ B_ε(γ(φ)) = spt C ∩ B_ε(γ(φ)), so γ(φ) ∈ spt C. Since γ(φ) → a as φ ↑ φ* and spt C is closed (d), a ∈ spt C.
4. (Density k at a, by the sector lemma.) Let e_a := sin φ*·z − cos φ*·e. Then a, e_a ∈ Q, |a| = |e_a| = 1 and ⟨a, e_a⟩ = cos φ* sin φ* − sin φ* cos φ* = 0. For every ψ ∈ ℝ, cos ψ·a + sin ψ·e_a = (cos ψ cos φ* + sin ψ sin φ*)·z + (cos ψ sin φ* − sin ψ cos φ*)·e = γ(φ* − ψ). Let t > 0 and 0 < ψ < φ*. Then φ* − ψ ∈ (0, φ*), so Good(γ(φ* − ψ)) holds with some ε. As γ(φ* − ψ) ∈ spt C ∩ B_ε(γ(φ* − ψ)), HasMassDensity C γ(φ* − ψ) k, hence HasMassDensity C (t·(cos ψ·a + sin ψ·e_a)) k by (c). Moreover spt C ∩ B_{tε}(t·γ(φ* − ψ)) ⊆ Q: if x belongs to the left side, then t⁻¹x ∈ spt C by (c) and |t⁻¹x − γ(φ* − ψ)| < ε, so t⁻¹x ∈ spt C ∩ B_ε(γ(φ* − ψ)) = Q ∩ B_ε(γ(φ* − ψ)) and x = t·(t⁻¹x) ∈ Q. Together with finrank Q = 2, k ≥ 1, a ∈ spt C (step 3) and φ* > 0, all hypotheses of the parent's sibling prerequisite Submission.idtp_cone_sector_endpoint_density (with Q, a, e := e_a, δ := φ*, k, and r := tε) hold, and it gives HasMassDensity C a k.
5. (Constant density near a.) Since 0 < φ* < L, a = γ(φ*) ∈ spt C and HasMassDensity C a k, hypothesis (ii) gives δ > 0 and k' ∈ ℕ with HasMassDensity C y k' for all y ∈ spt C ∩ B_δ(a). Taking y = a and using (a) with step 4, k' = k.
6. (The plane at a is Q.) As a ∈ spt C, a ≠ 0 (|a| = 1) and δ > 0, the parent's sibling prerequisite Submission.idtp_cone_constant_density_planar (p := a, k := k, δ) gives δ' > 0 and a linear subspace Q' with finrank Q' = 2, a ∈ Q' and spt C ∩ B_{δ'}(a) = Q' ∩ B_{δ'}(a). Let η := min(φ*, δ', 1)/2, so 0 < η ≤ 1/2, and φ := φ* − η ∈ [0, φ*). By step 3, γ(φ) ∈ spt C, and |γ(φ) − a| ≤ η < δ' by (b), so γ(φ) ∈ Q'. By step 4 (with ψ := η), γ(φ) = cos η·a + sin η·e_a with sin η > 0 (0 < η < π), so e_a = (sin η)⁻¹·(γ(φ) − cos η·a) ∈ Q'. Thus a, e_a ∈ Q ∩ Q'. Being orthonormal, a and e_a are linearly independent, so span{a, e_a} is 2-dimensional and contained in both Q and Q'; since finrank Q = finrank Q' = 2, Q = span{a, e_a} = Q'.
7. (Contradiction.) Let ε := min(δ, δ') > 0. Then spt C ∩ B_ε(a) = (spt C ∩ B_{δ'}(a)) ∩ B_ε(a) = Q ∩ B_ε(a), and every y ∈ spt C ∩ B_ε(a) satisfies HasMassDensity C y k' with k' = k (step 5). So Good(a) holds, contradicting step 2. Hence A = ∅, i.e. Good(γ(φ)) holds for every φ ∈ [0, L), which is the claim. ∎

If the claim fails, the first failure parameter φ* lies in (0, L), Good holds on [0, φ*), and a := γ(φ*) ∈ spt C because spt C is closed.
The backward sector at a (a, e_a orthonormal in Q; cone dilation from idtp_tdc_cone_dilation) satisfies the hypotheses of idtp_cone_sector_endpoint_density, so HasMassDensity C a k.

Hypothesis (ii) makes the density locally constant (equal to k) near a, and idtp_cone_constant_density_planar gives a local plane at a, which must be Q since it contains a and nearby points of the arc.
Hence Good(a) holds, contradicting the choice of φ*.

subproblem.title: The density of a 2-dimensional minimizing cone is locally constant on its support away from the vertex
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let C ∈ 𝒟_2(ℝ^P) be minimizing in ℝ^P (IsMinimizingIn C univ), with ∂C = 0 (BoundaryVanishes C) and a cone (IsConeCurrent C). Then for every p ∈ spt C with p ≠ 0 there are δ > 0 and k ∈ ℕ such that HasMassDensity C y k (i.e. Θ²(μ_C, y) = k) for every y ∈ spt C ∩ B_δ(p).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 2), IsMinimizingIn C univ → BoundaryVanishes C → IsConeCurrent C → ∀ p ∈ C.support, p ≠ 0 → ∃ (δ : ℝ) (k : ℕ), 0 < δ ∧ ∀ y ∈ C.support, y ∈ ball p δ → HasMassDensity C y k
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: paragraph (M) and steps 1–6 of the parent proof (its jump set J is shown to be empty; Departure [D3]: the book, chapter-07.txt lines 497–510, only cites [Whi82] for the classification of 2-dimensional area minimizing cones; cf. F. Morgan, Math. Ann. 261 (1982) 101–110). Steps 4 and 6 of the parent proof are packaged in the sibling idtp_tdc_arc_continuation and the finite-mass count of its step 5 in the sibling idtp_tdc_no_infinite_planar_pieces. Notation: 𝕊 := {x ∈ ℝ^P : |x| = 1}; B_r(x) = ball x r; H² = μHE[2]; M_W = massOn.
0. Facts. (a) Uniqueness of densities: HasMassDensity C y θ and HasMassDensity C y θ' imply θ = θ' (both are ≥ 0, limits in the Hausdorff space [0, ∞] are unique, and ENNReal.ofReal is injective on [0, ∞)). (b) Uniqueness of planes: if Q₁, Q₂ are linear subspaces, x ∈ Q₁, t > 0 and Q₁ ∩ B_t(x) = Q₂ ∩ B_t(x), then Q₁ = Q₂. [x ∈ Q₁ ∩ B_t(x) ⊆ Q₂; for v ∈ Q₁ and 0 < s < t/(|v| + 1), x + s·v ∈ Q₁ ∩ B_t(x) ⊆ Q₂, so s·v ∈ Q₂ and v ∈ Q₂; symmetrically Q₂ ⊆ Q₁.] (c) C is integer multiplicity (first component of IsMinimizingIn C univ), so the sibling idtp_tdc_cone_dilation gives, for s > 0 and all x, θ: s·x ∈ spt C ⟺ x ∈ spt C, and HasMassDensity C (s·x) θ ⟺ HasMassDensity C x θ. (d) spt C is closed (the complement of the open zero region). (e) For w ∈ 𝕊 and y ≠ 0: |y/|y| − w| ≤ |y/|y| − y| + |y − w| = ||y| − |w|| + |y − w| ≤ 2|y − w|.
1. Suppose, for a contradiction, that some p₀ ∈ spt C with p₀ ≠ 0 admits no δ > 0 and k ∈ ℕ as in the claim.
2. (Integer densities; P ≥ 2.) For q ∈ spt C ∖ {0}, the parent's sibling prerequisite Submission.idtp_cone_tangent_cone_planar (with λ_j := 1/(j + 1) > 0, λ_j → 0) gives an orthonormal family τ : Fin 2 → ℝ^P and c ∈ ℤ with |c| ≥ 1 and HasMassDensity C q |c|. Applied at q = p₀, the orthonormal (hence linearly independent) family τ shows P = finrank ℝ^P ≥ 2.
3. (Monotonicity.) Since 1 ≤ 2 ≤ P, the cross-branch theorem Submission.dimred_minimizing_monotonicity applies with n := 2, d := P, U := N := ℝ^P and T := C: ℝ^P is open; IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 P ℝ^P holds (for every y take V := W := ℝ^P and ψ := id, which is C², injective, with ψ(V) = W ∩ ℝ^P, V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) = K compact for every compact K, and injective derivative id); (closure ℝ^P ∖ ℝ^P) ∩ ℝ^P = ∅; C is minimizing in ℝ^P ∩ ℝ^P = ℝ^P; spt C ⊆ ℝ^P ∩ ℝ^P; BoundaryVanishes C. Its part (iii) gives Θ : ℝ^P → ℝ with HasMassDensity C y Θ(y) for every y and Θ upper semicontinuous on ℝ^P. By step 2 and (a), for q ∈ spt C ∖ {0}, Θ(q) = κ(q) for a natural number κ(q) ≥ 1. By (c) and (a), Θ(s·x) = Θ(x) for all s > 0 and x.
4. (The jump set.) Let J := {q ∈ spt C ∖ {0} : for every δ > 0 some y ∈ spt C ∩ B_δ(q) has Θ(y) ≠ Θ(q)}. If q ∈ spt C ∖ {0} and q ∉ J, there is δ > 0 with Θ(y) = Θ(q) = κ(q) for every y ∈ spt C ∩ B_δ(q), i.e. HasMassDensity C y κ(q) there, so the claim holds at q with k := κ(q). Hence p₀ ∈ J. J is dilation invariant: if q ∈ J and s > 0, then s·q ∈ spt C ∖ {0} by (c), and for δ > 0 a point y ∈ spt C ∩ B_{δ/s}(q) with Θ(y) ≠ Θ(q) gives s·y ∈ spt C ∩ B_δ(s·q) with Θ(s·y) = Θ(y) ≠ Θ(q) = Θ(s·q). Thus b' := p₀/|p₀| ∈ J ∩ 𝕊.
5. (A jump point of locally minimal density.) The set {κ(q) : q ∈ J ∩ 𝕊 ∩ B_{1/8}(b')} of natural numbers is nonempty (it contains κ(b')); let m₀ be its least element, attained at b ∈ J ∩ 𝕊 ∩ B_{1/8}(b'). Since Θ(b) = m₀ < m₀ + 1 and Θ is upper semicontinuous at b, there is r₀ > 0 with Θ(y) < m₀ + 1 for every y ∈ B_{r₀}(b). Let r := min(r₀, 1/8 − |b − b'|, 1/2) > 0, so B_r(b) ⊆ B_{1/8}(b'). (5a) If y ∈ spt C ∩ B_r(b), then |y| ≥ 1 − |y − b| > 1/2, so y ≠ 0, Θ(y) = κ(y) ∈ ℕ and κ(y) < m₀ + 1, i.e. κ(y) ≤ m₀. (5b) If q ∈ J ∩ 𝕊 ∩ B_r(b), then κ(q) ≥ m₀ by minimality (q ∈ B_{1/8}(b')) and κ(q) ≤ m₀ by (5a), so κ(q) = m₀.
6. (Light points accumulate at b.) Let r' := r/2. For every η ∈ (0, r'/2) there is z ∈ (spt C ∩ 𝕊) ∖ J with |z − b| < η and κ(z) < m₀. Indeed, b ∈ J gives y ∈ spt C ∩ B_{η/2}(b) with Θ(y) ≠ Θ(b) = m₀, and κ(y) < m₀ by (5a) (η/2 < r). Let z := y/|y|. Then z ∈ spt C by (c), |z| = 1, |z − b| ≤ 2|y − b| < η < r by (e), and Θ(z) = Θ(y) < m₀; if z ∈ J, (5b) would give κ(z) = m₀, so z ∉ J. For each i ∈ ℕ fix such a point z_i for η_i := r'/(4(i + 1)) and let k_i := κ(z_i); then 1 ≤ k_i < m₀ and |z_i − b| < η_i → 0.
7. (Planes at the light points.) Fix i. Since z_i ∈ spt C ∖ {0} and z_i ∉ J, step 4 gives δ_i > 0 with HasMassDensity C y k_i for every y ∈ spt C ∩ B_{δ_i}(z_i). The parent's sibling prerequisite Submission.idtp_cone_constant_density_planar (p := z_i, k := k_i, δ := δ_i) gives δ'_i > 0 and a linear subspace Q_i with finrank Q_i = 2, z_i ∈ Q_i and spt C ∩ B_{δ'_i}(z_i) = Q_i ∩ B_{δ'_i}(z_i). Choose e_i ∈ Q_i with |e_i| = 1 and ⟨z_i, e_i⟩ = 0 (Gram–Schmidt: if (u, v) is a basis of Q_i, then u − ⟨u, z_i⟩z_i and v − ⟨v, z_i⟩z_i lie in Q_i, are orthogonal to z_i, and are not both 0 because u, v are not both multiples of z_i; normalize a nonzero one). For w ∈ ℝ^P let Good_i(w) mean: there is ε > 0 with spt C ∩ B_ε(w) = Q_i ∩ B_ε(w) and HasMassDensity C y k_i for every y ∈ spt C ∩ B_ε(w).
8. (Long light arcs.) Let L := r'/2. Apply the sibling idtp_tdc_arc_continuation to (Q_i, z_i, e_i, k_i, L) and to (Q_i, z_i, −e_i, k_i, L) (−e_i ∈ Q_i is also a unit vector orthogonal to z_i). Its hypotheses hold: C is minimizing in ℝ^P with ∂C = 0 and is a cone; finrank Q_i = 2; z_i, ±e_i ∈ Q_i are orthonormal; k_i ≥ 1; (i) holds with ε := min(δ_i, δ'_i); for (ii), let 0 < φ < L and a := cos φ·z_i + sin φ·(±e_i) with a ∈ spt C and HasMassDensity C a k_i. Then |a| = 1 and |a − z_i| ≤ φ (|a − z_i|² = 2 − 2cos φ = 4sin²(φ/2) ≤ φ²), so |a − b| < φ + η_i < r'/2 + r'/2 = r' < r. If a ∈ J, then (5b) gives Θ(a) = κ(a) = m₀, while (a) gives Θ(a) = k_i < m₀; so a ∉ J, and step 4 gives δ > 0 with HasMassDensity C y κ(a) for every y ∈ spt C ∩ B_δ(a), which is (ii) with k' := κ(a). The sibling yields Good_i(cos φ·z_i + sin φ·e_i) for every φ ∈ (−L, L) (for φ < 0 use −e_i and −φ).
9. (Discs of good points.) Let ρ₀ := min(1/2, r'/8) > 0 and D_i := Q_i ∩ B_{ρ₀}(z_i). Claim: Good_i(x) for every x ∈ D_i. Let x ∈ D_i; then 1/2 < |x| < 3/2, x̂ := x/|x| ∈ Q_i ∩ 𝕊, and |x̂ − z_i| ≤ 2|x − z_i| < 2ρ₀ ≤ r'/4 by (e). Since (z_i, e_i) is an orthonormal basis of Q_i, x̂ = α·z_i + β·e_i with α² + β² = 1; choose φ ∈ (−π, π] with cos φ = α and sin φ = β (φ := arg(α + iβ)). Then |x̂ − z_i|² = 2 − 2cos φ = 4sin²(|φ|/2), and Jordan's inequality sin u ≥ (2/π)u for 0 ≤ u ≤ π/2 (Mathlib Real.mul_le_sin) with u = |φ|/2 gives |x̂ − z_i| ≥ (2/π)|φ|, so |φ| ≤ (π/2)|x̂ − z_i| < πr'/8 < r'/2 = L. By step 8, Good_i(x̂) holds with some ε. Let s := |x|. By (c), y ∈ spt C ∩ B_{sε}(x) iff y/s ∈ spt C ∩ B_ε(x̂) = Q_i ∩ B_ε(x̂) iff y ∈ Q_i ∩ B_{sε}(x); so spt C ∩ B_{sε}(x) = Q_i ∩ B_{sε}(x). For such y, HasMassDensity C (y/s) k_i, hence HasMassDensity C y k_i by (c). So Good_i(x) holds with sε.
10. (Local mass bound.) Let x ∈ D_i and let ε_x witness Good_i(x). Then x ∈ spt C (x ∈ Q_i ∩ B_{ε_x}(x)) and x ≠ 0, so Submission.idtp_cone_constant_density_planar (p := x, k := k_i, δ := ε_x) gives δ''_x > 0 and a subspace Q''_x with spt C ∩ B_{δ''_x}(x) = Q''_x ∩ B_{δ''_x}(x) and M_W(C) = k_i·H²(W ∩ Q''_x) for every open W ⊆ B_{δ''_x}(x). With t := min(ε_x, δ''_x): Q_i ∩ B_t(x) = spt C ∩ B_t(x) = Q''_x ∩ B_t(x) and x ∈ Q_i, so Q''_x = Q_i by (b). Hence for every open W ⊆ B_t(x): H²(W ∩ Q_i) ≤ k_i·H²(W ∩ Q_i) = M_W(C), as k_i ≥ 1.
11. (Disjoint discs.) If Q_i ≠ Q_j, then D_i ∩ D_j = ∅: for x ∈ D_i ∩ D_j, step 9 gives Good_i(x) and Good_j(x); with t the smaller of the two radii, Q_i ∩ B_t(x) = spt C ∩ B_t(x) = Q_j ∩ B_t(x) and x ∈ Q_i, so Q_i = Q_j by (b).
12. (Each plane occurs finitely often.) Suppose Q' is a subspace such that I := {i : Q_i = Q'} is infinite. The points z_i, i ∈ I, lie in the closed set Q' (Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional) and converge to b, so b ∈ Q'. Choose i ∈ I with η_i < ρ₀; then |b − z_i| < ρ₀, so b ∈ D_i, and Good_i(b) holds by step 9 with some ε: HasMassDensity C y k_i for all y ∈ spt C ∩ B_ε(b). As b ∈ spt C, (a) gives Θ(b) = k_i and Θ(y) = k_i = Θ(b) for all y ∈ spt C ∩ B_ε(b), so b ∉ J — contradicting b ∈ J. Hence every fibre {i : Q_i = Q'} is finite.
13. (Infinitely many distinct planes.) Let i_0 := 0 and, recursively, i_{l+1} := the least i with Q_i ∉ {Q_{i_0}, …, Q_{i_l}}; it exists because {i : Q_i ∈ {Q_{i_0}, …, Q_{i_l}}} is a finite union of finite fibres (step 12) while ℕ is infinite. The planes Q*_l := Q_{i_l} (l ∈ ℕ) are pairwise distinct.
14. (Contradiction.) Apply the sibling idtp_tdc_no_infinite_planar_pieces to C, the families Q*_l and z*_l := z_{i_l}, ρ := ρ₀ and R := 1: C is integer multiplicity; ρ₀ > 0; finrank Q*_l = 2; z*_l ∈ Q*_l; |z*_l| = 1 ≤ 1; for l ≠ l', Q*_l ≠ Q*_{l'}, so the discs Q*_l ∩ B_{ρ₀}(z*_l) = D_{i_l} and D_{i_{l'}} are disjoint by step 11; and every w ∈ D_{i_l} has ε > 0 with H²(W ∩ Q*_l) ≤ M_W(C) for every open W ⊆ B_ε(w) by step 10. The sibling yields False. This contradiction proves the claim at every p ∈ spt C ∖ {0}. ∎

If J ≠ ∅, pick b ∈ J ∩ 𝕊 of locally minimal density m₀ and r > 0 with Θ ≤ m₀ on spt C ∩ B_r(b) and Θ = m₀ on J ∩ 𝕊 ∩ B_r(b).
Light points z_i ∉ J of density k_i < m₀ accumulate at b, and each has a local plane Q_i (idtp_cone_constant_density_planar).

Discs on distinct planes are disjoint, and each plane occurs only finitely often (otherwise b would be Good); infinitely many disjoint discs contradict idtp_tdc_no_infinite_planar_pieces.
